procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The wife filed a Transfer Petition (C) No. 2043 of 2023 in the Supreme Court under Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, seeking to transfer the Maintenance Case No.326/2023 from Ranchi. During the pendency of the petition, the parties decided to resolve the dispute and filed a joint application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India. The Supreme Court allowed the application under Article 142 and disposed of the Transfer Petition.

directions: The application filed under Article 142 of the Constitution is allowed.
The three cases filed by the parties against each other stand quashed.

issue.issue_text: Whether the joint application filed by the parties under Article 142 of the Constitution, seeking to quash the three cases filed against each other based on a settlement, should be allowed.

facts: During the pendency of a transfer petition, the parties involved decided to resolve their disputes.
They filed a joint application under Article 142 of the Constitution, seeking to quash three cases they had filed against each other.
The parties stated that they filed the application on their own free will, without any coercion or undue influence, and agreed to abide by its terms.
law: Article 142 of the Constitution of India grants the Supreme Court the power to pass such orders as are necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.
application: The Supreme Court took the joint application on record and reviewed its terms and conditions.
The Court found the terms of the settlement to be lawful.
The Court determined that there was no legal impediment to accepting the terms of the joint application.
reasoning.conclusion: Based on the finding that the settlement was lawful and voluntarily entered into by the parties, the Supreme Court allowed the joint application and, exercising its powers under Article 142, quashed the three cases the parties had filed against each other.
